ROLL CALL: At 6:02 p.m., on Monday, January 25, 2021 the Alhambra City Council met via
video conference, and via teleconference.

COUNCIL PRESENT via video conference: LEE, MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER,
PÉREZ
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present physically, via teleconference, and via video conference: City Manager
Binnquist, City Attorney Montes, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager Tran,
City Clerk Myles, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of Public Works/ Utilities Ray, Director of
Parks and Recreation Macias, Marketing and Communications Specialist Nguyen, Management
Analyst Cuevas, Director of Community Development Castagnola, Deputy Director of
Community Development Reynoso, Fire Chief Phelps, Police Chief Vu, Director of Human
Resources Ko

FLAG SALUTE:  Mayor Pérez

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M21-9

The City Clerk reported that she duly gave notice of the regular meeting of the City Council
being held pursuant to the order of the Mayor in accordance with Section 54955 and 54956 of
the Government Code of the State of California.

READING OF ORDINANCE TITLES

Government Code Section 36934 requires that all ordinances be read in full prior to City Council
taking action on the ordinance. By listing the ordinance title on the Council agenda, Council may
determine that the title has been read.

Action Taken:  On motion of Ms. LEE, seconded by Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER, the City
Council determined that the titles to all ordinances which appeared on this public agenda had
been read, and waived further reading. Hearing no objections, the Mayor so ordered.

PUBLIC HEARING

1.  ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION ESTABLISHING A FEE SCHEDULE IN-LIEU OF
  PRODUCING AFFORDABLE HOUSING UNITS AS REQUIRED BY ALHAMBRA
  MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 23.89 - INCLUSIONARY HOUSING - F2M18-35,

  1
1-25-21
   N2M21-5, R2M21-2
  This was the time and place set by Notice No. N2M21-5 for the City Council to hold a
  public hearing to consider adoption of a proposed resolution to create a fee schedule in-
  lieu of producing affordable housing units as required by Alhambra Municipal Code
  (AMC) Chapter 23.89 - Inclusionary Housing. Director of Community Development
  CASTAGNOLA delivered a staff report and a presentation which is on file in the City
  Clerk’s office. On September28, 2020, the City Council adopted Ordinance O2M20-
  4778 - Inclusionary Housing, amending AMC Chapter 23.89 requiring affordable
  housing units for all newly constructed dwelling units to be sold or rented and Resolution
  R2M20-32 adopting the Inclusionary Housing Regulations. AMC Chapter
  23.89.050(A)(1) required the City Council to establish an in-lieu fee as an alternative to
  producing affordable units for projects of 20 units or less with procedures set by the
  Regulation Section IV. On October 1, 2020, the City Council approved a contract with
  Keyser Marston Associates (KMA) to provide an analysis to assist the City in
  establishing a recommended in-lieu fee schedule for projects subject to the
  requirements of the Inclusionary Housing Ordinance. The proposed In-Lieu Fee
  schedule would be proportional to the number of units and total square foot of saleable
  or leasable area of newly constructed dwelling units up to a maximum of $30.00 per
  square foot of saleable area for ownership housing development and a maximum of
  $14.30 per square foot of leasable area for apartment housing development as follows:

  Recommended Inclusionary Housing In-Lieu Fee Schedule Per Square Foot of
  Saleable or Leasable Area
  Units  Condominiums  Apartments  Units  Condominiums  Apartments
  Provided  Ownership  Rental  Provided  Ownership  Rental
  5  $1.88  $0.89  13  $16.88  $8.04
  6  $3.75  $1.79  14  $18.75  $8.94
  7  $5.63  $2.68  15  $20.63  $9.83
  8  $7.50  $3.58  16  $22.50  $10.73
  9  $9.38  $4.47  17  $24.38  $11.62
  10  $11.25  $5.36  18  $26.25  $12.51
  11  $13.13  $6.26  19  $28.13  $13.41
  12  $15.00  $7.15  20  $30.00  $14.30

  Per the Inclusionary Housing Regulation Section IV(A)(3), the in-lieu fee schedule shall
  be adopted every five years based upon a real estate market study and shall be
  adjusted annually based upon changes in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for the Los
  Angeles- Long Beach Standard Metropolitan Statistical Area (LA-LB SMSA), the House
  Price Index for the LA-LB SMSA, a hybrid of these two indices, or some other
  appropriate housing market index. Revenue collected from the in-lieu fee would be
  deposited in Inclusionary Housing Trust Fund for the purpose of supporting the
  production of affordable housing units.

  Opened the Public Hearing: Mayor PÉREZ opened the public hearing.

  Public Comment received via email on file in the City Clerk’s office: Shirley TATSUNO
  wrote regarding her concerns with the in-lieu fee schedule.

  Closed the Public Hearing: After receiving public comment, Mayor PÉREZ closed the
  public hearing.

  2
1-25-21
   Discussion: Council supported the Resolution and commended staff for their efforts.
  Councilmember MALONEY and Mr. CASTAGNOLA discussed adjustments that could
  potentially be made to the fee schedule after a yearly review.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M21-2 entitled: A
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of Alhambra, State of California, establishing
  an Inclusionary Housing In-Lieu Fee Schedule

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

PRESENTATIONS

2.  2020 CITY ACCOMPLISHMENTS REPORT - F2M18-35

  Assistant City Manager GARCIA presented the 2020 Accomplishments Report which
  highlighted many of the past year’s achievements. The presentation is on file in the City
  Clerk’s office. The accomplishments aligned with the City’s Strategic Plan, which was
  prioritized to reflect the community’s core values. The Report was intended to heighten
  community awareness of new and ongoing activities and projects.

  Discussion: Council commended staff for their efforts and spoke positively regarding
  the accomplishments of the City in spite of the challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic.
  Councilmember LEE suggested that the report or a summary of the report should be
  translated into major languages for non-English speaking residents.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the informational report.

3.  COUNCIL DIRECTION ON STORY PARK LAND PARCELS - F2M21-22

  Director of Parks and Recreation MACIAS delivered a staff report and displayed a map
  of the park land and adjacent lots, which is on file in the City Clerk’s office. City staff
  received a complaint from a resident of N. Story Place regarding leaves falling from an
  oak tree from an adjacent parcel creating a hazard. The resident stated the area had
  previously been cleaned by City staff (eight to ten years ago). Code enforcement staff
  researched the issue and determined the parcel was, in fact, part of the Story Park
  property boundaries. The parcels are landlocked and have been inaccessible for many
  years. Only the property owners have direct access to the land. The parcels of land sit
  on the eastern side of Story Park, separated by the San Pasqual Wash. Staff
  considered options for the Story Park parcels. At this time, staff sought direction from
  the City Council on the following two considerations: a) Keep the parcels status quo and
  begin maintenance of the properties east of the San Pasqual Wash, as needed, or b)
  Direct staff to have a land survey and appraisals performed and research the process to
  vacate the inaccessible parkland.

  Discussion: Council discussed the proposals and options available. Councilmember
  MALONEY suggested placing protections on the existing mature trees on the land
  before any consideration of transferring ownership. Council agreed to have the land
  surveyed and appraised in order to ultimately vacate the parcels.

  3
1-25-21
   Action Taken:  City Council directed staff to conduct a land survey and have
  appraisals performed and research the process to vacate the inaccessible parkland;
  and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  MALONEY, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

4.  SELECTION OF A FRANCHISE WASTE HAULER FOR RESIDENTIAL AND
  COMMERCIAL INTEGRATED SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT SERVICES - F2M20-
  39, F2M10-26, F94-80, RFP2M20-10

  Management Analyst CUEVAS delivered a staff report and introduced Laith EZZET and
  Debbie MORRIS of the consultants HF&H who delivered a presentation, a copy of which
  is on file in the City Clerk’s office. At the April 27, 2020 City Council Meeting, the City
  Council approved the distribution of an RFP (RFP2M20-10) for a combined residential
  and commercial integrated solid waste management services agreement. On April 28,
  2020, the RFP was publicly released and emailed to a list of solid waste haulers as well
  as placed on the City’s website to enable additional solid waste haulers the opportunity
  to review and respond to the City’s RFP. The initial due date for proposals was July 30,
  2020, but was extended to August 27, 2020, to allow interested proposers more time to
  respond to the RFP requirements. Upon the close of the RFP submission deadline, the
  City received seven proposals from solid waste haulers. Over the past several months,
  following the receipt of proposals, a comprehensive evaluation of each solid waste
  hauler’s proposal was conducted, including a review of proposed rates and financials to
  determine fiscal stability of each hauler, service levels and requirements for both the
  residential and commercial sectors in the City, proposed service enhancements and
  each proposal’s compliance with current and upcoming State mandates based upon the
  RFP terms and scope of work. Each proposal was evaluated according to the base
  criteria established in the RFP, which included: Proposer’s Qualifications; Technical
  Qualifications; Exceptions to the Terms and Conditions; Financial Resources; Costs;
  and, Employment of Prior Contract’s Workers. All of the proposals received by the City
  met the minimum RFP requirements. As reflected in the evaluation report (attached) and
  based on Option 2 (Source Separated processing), and as measured by total rate
  revenues and the lowest residential monthly rates for cart customers, two proposers -
  Athens Services and Republic Services - emerged as top considerations.

  Discussion: Councilmember LEE discussed American Reclamation’s proposal to offer

  6
1-25-21
   street sweeping services as compared to services offered by Republic Services with Mr.
  EZZAT and Mr. CUEVAS. She went on to discuss the $1 million grant offered by
  American Reclamation with Mr. EZZAT. Ms. LEE further discussed the anti-scavenging
  assistance section in the services agreement with Ms. MORRIS. Ms. LEE went on to
  express concerns based on Athens’s history in the City and advocated for consideration
  of American Reclamation instead. She made a motion for Council to select Option B to
  negotiate an agreement with Republic Services and American Reclamation, and to
  include free paper document shredding services in the contract. Mr. EZZAT and Ms.
  MORRIS clarified that this service was in the RFP and draft contract as an annual paper
  shredding event open to residents. Having no second, Ms. Lee’s motion did not proceed.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. EZZAT discussed the RFP selection
  process and the priorities discussed with the City. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER continued
  to discuss SB 1383, the goals of the California law, and specifically food waste and food
  waste prevention. She went on to discuss the many ways in which Republic Services
  had been active members in the community and reported on the various events,
  particularly to provide relief during the COVID-19 pandemic, that they attended or
  donated services to. She continued to speak positively about Republic Services, their
  facilities, their support offered to their employees and their families, and the many
  services that they provided the City of Alhambra. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER motioned to
  proceed with Option 1 and award a contract to Republic Services.

  Councilmember MAZA thanked all the haulers that participated in City events and
  commended the work of HF&H during the RFP process. He referred to the lower than
  expected prices quoted in some of the proposals, but noted that it would be unfair to
  rebid the contract and try to negotiate lower prices with other vendors after all bids were
  submitted. He stressed the importance of the contract and the need to maximize all the
  benefits to the City and meet all the needs of the residents. Mr. Maza supported Option
  2 and the Source Separated processing to better meet the new environmental demands.
  He stressed that there should not be any renegotiation of the contract for pricing once it
  was awarded. He reasoned that should Council vote to proceed with Option 2 and in
  order to maximize the benefits to the community that the chosen hauler commit to a
  strong informational campaign for the community regarding new regulations under SB
  1383. He reviewed the contract enhancements submitted, and suggested adding five
  annual clean-ups of the Alhambra Business Corridors on Main Street and Valley
  Boulevard. He also suggested the selected hauler provide a locally present customer
  service office dedicated to the City of Alhambra.

  Councilmember MALONEY commended staff and the consultants during the RFP
  process, thanked the bidders for their proposals, and stated that good faith should be
  offered to all bidders regardless of past history. He also discussed the food recovery
  requirements of SB 1383, the tiered responsibilities and responses of the City, and the
  responsibilities of the contracted hauler with Ms. MORRIS, Mr. CUEVAS and MR.
  EZZAT. Mr. MALONEY next discussed the enforcement stage and potential penalties
  under SB1383 with Ms. MORRIS. Mr. MALONEY further discussed the current and
  projected diversion rates with Ms. MORRIS. Mr. MALONEY also discussed the state of
  plastic recycling with regards to changes in the overseas recyclers and the diversion
  rates with Ms. Morris. Mr. MALONEY went on to discuss the fuel used by waste vehicles
  and the differences between renewable natural gas and compressed natural gas with
  Ms. MORRIS. Ms. Morris explained the ways in which changing to renewable gas would
  help the City reach certain goals under SB1383. Mr. MALONEY discussed the bidding

  7
1-25-21
   process should negotiations fail with any of the other bidders with Mr. EZZAT.

  Mr. MALONEY agreed with Mr. Maza’s comments and initially supported Option 2 to
  better commit to the direction of State environmental compliance and in order to reduce
  the amount of waste. He went on to further discuss the food waste requirements.
  However, he went on to review the rates proposed under Option 2 by Athens and
  Republic and reasoned that it made sense to choose the lowest cost to the residents
  who may already may be struggling during the COVID-19 pandemic. He went on to refer
  to the time constraints due to the end date of the current contract and the
  implementation deadline of SB 1383 and argued that Option 2 may require more time
  than available to establish separate waste systems. He concluded that it would be more
  expedient to choose Option 1 and negotiate exclusively with Republic Services. He went
  on to discuss the exceptions raised by Republic Services under their exclusive bid with
  Mr. EZZAT, provided under Attachment 7. Mr. Ezzat suggested that the City not
  negotiate with flexibility on the exception to Article 6.5 and suggested that the City
  continue to negotiate with Republic Services before finalizing the contract decision. Mr.
  MALONEY also discussed Republic Services’ exception to Article 10, “The City’s Right
  to Perform Services” with Ms. MORRIS. Mr. MALONEY continued to express his
  concerns regarding Republic Service improving their response time to the residents.

  David CANNON, General Manager at Republic Services, responded to concerns raised
  by Mr. Maloney and stated that all exceptions were negotiable. He requested more
  clarification on Article 10 and explained the company’s concerns with regard to Article
  6.5. He also clarified that with regards to enhancing customer service, Republic Services
  would now handle billing for customers and they would have greater accessibility to
  communicating directly with residents. Additionally, he stated that their proposal stated
  that a representative would be present in the City to deal directly with customers. Mr.
  MAZA further discussed Republic Services’ exception to SERFF being used under the
  City contract. Mr. CANNON responded that based on the diversion assumptions, the
  City should move towards a 3 bin solution which would utilize SERFF less. He went on
  to explain in greater detail. Mr. MAZA referred to Mr. Maloney’s comment, and asked if
  Republic Services could guarantee that they would be able to enter into a contract as
  proposed as quickly as possible to meet the time constraints. Mr. CANNON stated that
  aside from minor language clarification, that there were no obstacles to moving forward
  with the proposed contract. Mr. CANNON addressed public comment regarding use of
  electric vehicles and clarified the use of vehicles in other states. Mr. MALONEY
  discussed the enhancements offered by other bidders and asked if they could negotiate
  similar enhancements with Republic. Mr. CANNON agreed with his comments and
  stated that many of those services were offered as standard services in their contract
  and not as enhancements. Mr. MAZA seconded Ms. Andrade-Stadler’s motion, with the
  addition of contract enhancements proposed by Council during the meeting.

  Action Taken:  City Council selected Option 1 and awarded contract with
  Republic Services, adding contract enhancements; and directed staff to conduct
  contract negotiations and return at a future meeting for approval of final contract terms.

5.  RESOLUTION TO SUPPORT SPECIAL LEGISLATION TO AUTHORIZE THE CITY TO
  CONDUCT A CHARTER AMENDMENT ELECTION ON ANY ESTABLISHED
  ELECTION DATE SET FORTH IN ELECTIONS CODE SECTION 1000 TO ENABLE
  THE ALHAMBRA UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT’S TRANSITION TO A BY-TRUSTEE
  AREA ELECTION SYSTEM TO CONTINUE AND BE IN EFFECT FOR THE
  NOVEMBER 2022 GOVERNING BOARD ELECTIONS - F2M20-36, R2M21-3

  In January 2020, the Alhambra Unified School District Board requested that the City
  Council place a ballot measure on the November 2020 ballot to amend the Alhambra
  Charter to eliminate reference to the District in the Charter so that the District can
  proceed with the transition to by-district elections, as provided for under applicable
  governing State law. The District sought to make such a transition to ensure compliance
  with the California Voting Rights Act. The Alhambra City Council placed Measure G on
  the November ballot to effectuate the District’s request. Due to a County clerical order,
  Measure G was only submitted to the District voters living within City limits. Accordingly,
  it was necessary to conduct another election with regard to Measure G before the
  District could transition to by-district elections. Representatives of the County, District
  and City met and determined that pursuing special legislation to allow a special charter
  amendment election to occur at any established election date prior to November 2022,
  so that the District’s next elections could be conducted by-district, which would be what
  would have transpired had Measure G passed in November 2020, after being submitted
  to all of the voters within the District. The proposed resolution would express support for
  such legislation, and direct and authorize the City Manager and/or her designees to
  work with the District, County and State legislators to pursue the special legislation
  necessary to allow for another election.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M21-3 entitled: A
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of Alhambra to support special legislation to
  authorize the City of Alhambra to conduct a Charter Amendment Election on any
  established election date set forth in Elections Code Section 1000 to enable the
  Alhambra Unified School District’s transition to a by-trustee area election system to
  continue and be in effect for the November 2022 Governing Board Elections

1-25-21

7.  AUTHORIZE RFP: POLICE PARKING ENFORCEMENT SERVICES - F2M21-23,
  RFP2M21-3

  In December 2019, the parking enforcement company, Serco Inc. ended their contract
  with the City and Intercon Security Inc. assumed conducting parking services as of
  January 1, 2020. The contract with Intercon Security Inc. was set to end June 30, 2021
  and there were no provisions in the contract for an extension. Therefore, staff requested
  that the City Council authorize staff to circulate a Request for Proposals for a three (3)
  year contract to conduct parking enforcement services. Parking enforcement services
  included, but were not limited to, parking enforcement on street sweeping routes, timed
  parking zones, 72-hour parking violates, overnight parking violations, and radio calls
  regarding vehicles blocking driveways, blocking sidewalks, handicap parking violations,
  and any Alhambra Municipal Code parking violations.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to solicit proposals for a three (3)
  year contract to conduct parking enforcement services for the City of Alhambra; and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  for fiscal year 2020-2021. The City had the option to lease these rights to interested
  parties for a fee. The Kinneloa Irrigation District offered to lease 207 acre-feet of our

  10
1-25-21
   Raymond Basin water rights for $305.00 per acre-foot, for a total of $63,135. As such,

9.  AWARD CONTRACT: INTERIOR COATING OF TREATMENT VESSELS 202A AND
  207B AT THE GROUND WATER TREATMENT PLANT - F2M20-62, N2M20-123,
  C2M21-4, M2M21-10

  On September 14, 2020, the City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting
  Bids for the Interior Coating of Vessels 202A and 207B at the Groundwater Treatment
  Plant. Bids were opened by the City Clerk on December 3, 2020. Three bids were

14.  ANALYSIS OF IMPEDIMENTS TO FAIR HOUSING CHOICE - F2M20-58

  Under the 2015 Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing regulation, the Department of

  13
1-25-21
   Housing and Urban Development (HUD) previously required all entitlement jurisdictions
  that receive funding to affirmatively further fair housing by taking proactive steps to
  overcome housing discrimination and segregation. To help meet this expectation,
  jurisdictions conducted an Analysis of Impediments to Fair Housing Choice (AI) Study
  every five (5) years. The AI identified fair housing issues in the community and outlined
  goals and strategies to address issues. Staff anticipated submitting the draft AI to the
  City Council on August 10, 2020 with the 2020-2024 Consolidated Plan; however, on
  July 23, 2020, HUD issued a new rule entitled Preserving Community and Neighborhood
  Choice that terminated the 2015 Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing regulation and no
  longer required jurisdictions to conduct an AI in the foreseeable future or until the federal
  government reinstitutes the prior requirements. The new rule only required that
  participating jurisdictions certify active steps have been taken to promote fair housing
  and eliminate housing discrimination. At the time of HUD’s publication, HUD did not
  provide specific guidance on how to meet the new standards or how the City would be
  evaluated; therefore, this AI was submitted to help memorialize and certify the City’s
  efforts to address fair housing.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the Analysis of Impediments to Fair
  Housing Choice.

  3.32 TO CREATE THE SAFE CLEAN WATER MUNICIPAL PROGRAM FUND -
  F2M20-17, O2M21-4782, M2M21-8

  Section 3.32.010 of the Alhambra Municipal Code created and established the funds
  and account groups for the conduct and operation of the municipal fiscal affairs of the
  city government, including those funds established by the City Charter. The City would
  begin to receive the Safe Clean Water Municipal Program (SCW) funds from the Los
  Angeles County Flood Control District for Fiscal Year 2019-20. SCW has estimated the
  City would receive $860,000 of SCW funds in Fiscal Year 2020-21. The Los Angeles
  County Flood Control District (District) administers the SCW Program for the purpose of
  funding projects to increase stormwater and urban runoff capture as well as reduce
  stormwater and urban runoff pollution in the District. These funds were restricted and
  may only be expended for eligible costs. The creation of Section 3.32.149 for the Safe
  Clean Water Program was necessary to provide better tracking of funds received and
  related expenditures to ensure compliance with program requirements.

  Safe Clean Water Municipal Program
